results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 68 aligned summaries match their spec paragraphs' controlling ideas in the same order (the three callouts are unaligned front matter); only small drift, e.g. the outliner's p42 summary foregrounds the 'second order system' rule, which the spec's p42 also carries.
The cold reverse outline lists the spec's controlling ideas p01-p68 in spec order, section by section, with no missing, merged or reordered unit.

The only unit marked two_ideas is The Choices ¶8 (recommendation plus 'never let the warehouse system become a second order system'); the spec's p42 controlling idea deliberately joins the recommendation and its one rule with the Kestrel & Pine example, so the paragraph carries the declared single idea.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim: scene and WMS sections to S1 and S5, fulfillment order to S2, stock to S3, day to S5, wholesale to S4, choices and stages to S6, automation to S1/S2, In Practice to S5, failures to S2-S5; the Zalando ZEOS paragraph is the thinnest link (S6 via the uncountable location) but still traces.

Each table and figure is introduced or followed by a sentence saying what it shows (e.g. 'The table sets the four side by side: in every row the integration is the same contract'), quotations (GS1, Zalando) are glossed, and the DeHoratius figure is qualified; the scene's daily-rhythm table has only a lead-in ('Its daily rhythm below is illustrative'), which is thin but adequate since ¶4 uses its 21:00 wave.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary: 'similarly' (p02), 'Then Daniel shows... but' (p08 contrast), 'Those steps... lead to' (p13), 'for a physical reason' (p19), 'Besides its stock' (p28), 'With the contract in place' (p35), 'Back at Duiven, which has no robots' (in-practice), 'Beyond the Black Friday queue' (wrong); the Questions list (p67) relies on its heading for the cause_effect link, which is adequate.

Both readers describe the declared prerequisite order (problem/scene, then what a WMS does, then the contract, then options, scale, automation, worked cases, failures), with the interface subsections in the announced order; no section is unclear to both, and the material lost-thread points are recorded separately below.

results.finding: The introduction opens with a concrete puzzling scenario (the picker who finds no jacket) and moves to a specific claim; no placeholder, restated question, dictionary or 'dawn of man' opening.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion' or merely restate the thesis; it synthesizes the three opening faults into one cause and sorts what holds by how settled it is, with no new idea or body evidence.

What to Take Away ¶1 reads the missing jacket, Eva's Wednesday promise and the Black Friday queue as one failure ('a promise made from a copy or a sentence') and states the so-what: write the contract before buying a WMS, a 3PL or robots.
The conclusion's first sentence returns to 'The picker who found no jacket', the opening's element named in conclusion.callback.to, and names the warehouse fact each failure ignored.

The intro reader predicted the Duiven Black Friday opening, what a WMS does, the fulfillment order with acceptance, the stock count, cut-off/capacity/release feeding the promise, wholesale labels, choices and scale, automation, Eva's order, the failures, and Kestrel & Pine plus vendor/standards documentation as evidence: the substance of expected.

The reader places the fault in the order feed (one-at-a-time creation, several calls, vendor rate limit) and in a promise that ignored the queue, says the warehouse was never the limit, and names all four remedies: growing queue, batches within the limit, oldest-order age monitor, moving cut-off.

The reader says the idempotency key makes the WMS reuse the existing order (one jacket, alert on repeat) and that a cancellation after acceptance is a request the warehouse answers; if refused the order stays in progress, support tells the customer and the item returns.
The reader names the WMS, at pack time, from what was actually packed, never from the order or the ERP's view, citing the €14,200 ASN Chargeback and W6.
